CLAIM: The proposed system eliminates the need for a trusted third party in sealed-bid auctions.
ASSUMPTIONS: Ethereum blockchain is immutable, smart contracts execute as designed, Finance Intermediary (FI) is reliable.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Applies only to sealed-bid auctions implemented on Ethereum.

CLAIM: The system guarantees that the highest bidder wins the auction.
ASSUMPTIONS: Bidders submit valid bids, smart contract logic is correct, Ethereum network functions as expected.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Limited to sealed-bid auctions implemented using the proposed smart contract on Ethereum.

CLAIM: The system verifies that the winning bidder has sufficient funds to cover their bid.
ASSUMPTIONS: The Finance Intermediary (FI) provides accurate balance information, the smart contract can reliably access this information.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Relies on the integration with and reliability of the Finance Intermediary (FI).

CLAIM: Bid values are validated against FI account balances before on-chain submission.
ASSUMPTIONS: The Finance Intermediary (FI) provides accurate account balance information.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Account balance validation occurs before the bid deadline.

CLAIM: Blockchain immutability provides transparency in the auction process.
ASSUMPTIONS: All bids and auction outcomes are recorded on the blockchain.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Transparency limited to information recorded on the blockchain.

CLAIM: Existing sealed-bid auction systems rely on trusted third parties (TTP).
ASSUMPTIONS: Surveys/literature reviews accurately represent current auction practices.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Focuses on electronic/online sealed-bid auction systems.

CLAIM: The smart contract correctly implements the sealed-bid auction logic.
ASSUMPTIONS: Smart contract code has been formally verified.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Relies on correctness of the smart contract code.

CLAIM: The use of smart contracts increases transparency compared to traditional auctions.
ASSUMPTIONS: Traditional auctions do not offer equivalent transparency mechanisms.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Depends on the specific implementation of both the proposed and traditional auctions.

CLAIM: Ethereum can handle the transaction volume required for the auction use cases.
ASSUMPTIONS: Ethereum network has sufficient capacity.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Subject to Ethereum network congestion and gas fees.

CLAIM: The Finance Intermediary (FI) can accurately and reliably verify bidder funds.
ASSUMPTIONS: The FI has secure and accurate accounting systems.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Relies on the security and reliability of the FI.

CLAIM: Bidders trust the FI to accurately report their account balance.
ASSUMPTIONS: Bidders have a pre-existing relationship with the FI.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Trust depends on the reputation and regulatory oversight of the FI.

CLAIM: The system can be applied to product sales use cases.
ASSUMPTIONS: Products can be clearly defined and valued.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Limited to scenarios where product value is easily determined.

CLAIM: The system can be applied to Government procurement use cases.
ASSUMPTIONS: Government procurement processes are compatible with the proposed system.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Government regulations allow for smart contract based auctions.

CLAIM: The auction process is automated through the use of smart contracts.
ASSUMPTIONS: The smart contract code fully implements the auction logic.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Excludes any off-chain components or manual intervention.

CLAIM: The cost of running the auction is reduced compared to traditional auctions.
ASSUMPTIONS: The cost of gas fees on Ethereum is lower than the cost of TTP.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Cost comparison depends on the scale and frequency of auctions.

CLAIM: The proposed system eliminates the need for a trusted third party to execute sealed-bid auctions.
ASSUMPTIONS: Ethereum blockchain is immutable, smart contracts are correctly implemented, Finance Intermediary (FI) is honest
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Only applies to sealed-bid auctions, assumes reliable FI connection to Ethereum

CLAIM: The smart contract guarantees the highest bidder wins the auction.
ASSUMPTIONS: Smart contract code is correct and free of vulnerabilities, all bids are submitted on time.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Limited to the specific smart contract implementation described in the paper.

CLAIM: The system verifies that the winning bidder possesses sufficient funds to cover their bid.
ASSUMPTIONS: Finance Intermediary (FI) provides accurate balance information, funds are available at the time of settlement.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Relies on the FI's ability to accurately represent a bidder's financial status.

CLAIM: The system achieves transparency through the Ethereum blockchain.
ASSUMPTIONS: All bids and the winning bid are recorded publicly on the blockchain, users understand how to access and interpret blockchain data.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Transparency is limited to on-chain data; bidder identities may still be obscured.

CLAIM: The system is applicable to product sales.
ASSUMPTIONS: Product sale involves a single seller and multiple potential buyers.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Assumes the product is suitable for auction-style sales.

CLAIM: The system is applicable to government procurement.
ASSUMPTIONS: Government procurement processes can be adapted to a sealed-bid auction format.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Depends on government regulations and procurement policies.

CLAIM: Existing sealed-bid auction systems rely on trusted third parties (TTP).
ASSUMPTIONS: Traditional auction systems require a central authority to manage bids and determine the winner.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: May not apply to all types of auctions or specific implementations.

CLAIM: The Ethereum smart contract correctly implements the sealed-bid auction logic.
ASSUMPTIONS: The contract code has been thoroughly tested and verified to be bug-free.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Depends on the quality of the smart contract code and its deployment.

CLAIM: The Finance Intermediary (FI) accurately validates bid values against FI account balances before on-chain submission.
ASSUMPTIONS: FI has accurate and up-to-date information on bidder account balances.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Dependent on the FI's internal systems and security measures.

CLAIM: Bidders are guaranteed that their bids are kept secret until the reveal phase.
ASSUMPTIONS: Cryptographic techniques used to conceal bids are secure and correctly implemented.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Requires bidders to follow protocol for encryption and submission of bids.

CLAIM: The system can handle a large number of bids without significant performance degradation.
ASSUMPTIONS: Ethereum network has sufficient capacity to process transactions related to the auction.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Performance may be affected by network congestion or smart contract complexity.

CLAIM: The system reduces the potential for collusion among bidders.
ASSUMPTIONS: The anonymity provided by the system makes it more difficult for bidders to coordinate their bids.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Collusion is still possible, but it may be more challenging.

CLAIM: The use of Ethereum reduces the cost of conducting sealed-bid auctions compared to traditional methods.
ASSUMPTIONS: The cost of using Ethereum (gas fees) is lower than the fees charged by trusted third parties.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Depends on the cost of gas on the Ethereum network and the complexity of the smart contract.

CLAIM: The system is more resistant to fraud than existing sealed-bid auction systems.
ASSUMPTIONS: Blockchain immutability and smart contract enforcement reduce the opportunity for fraudulent activities.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Requires proper security measures to prevent attacks on the smart contract.

CLAIM: The system provides a tamper-proof record of all bids and the winning bid.
ASSUMPTIONS: The Ethereum blockchain is immutable and resistant to tampering.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Depends on the security of the Ethereum blockchain.

CLAIM: The proposed system eliminates the need for a trusted third party (TTP) in sealed-bid auctions.
ASSUMPTIONS: Ethereum blockchain is immutable, Smart contracts execute as designed.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Applies only to sealed-bid auctions implemented on Ethereum.

CLAIM: The system guarantees the highest bidder wins the auction.
ASSUMPTIONS: Bidders act rationally, Smart contract logic is correct.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Assumes no bugs in the smart contract implementation; Applies only to auctions where bids represent a higher value preference.

CLAIM: The system guarantees the winning bidder has sufficient funds to cover their bid.
ASSUMPTIONS: Finance Intermediary (FI) correctly validates account balances, FI doesn't collude.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Depends on the FI's validation accuracy and reliability.

CLAIM: The system increases transparency compared to traditional sealed-bid auctions.
ASSUMPTIONS: Blockchain immutability ensures bid history cannot be altered, Bid data is publicly accessible on the blockchain.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Limited to the transparency of bid submission and winner determination; Does not expose bidder identities.

CLAIM: The system is suitable for product sales use cases.
ASSUMPTIONS: Potential buyers are willing to use cryptocurrency for transactions, Transaction costs on Ethereum are reasonable.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Depends on product value and Ethereum gas fees at time of auction.

CLAIM: The system is suitable for government procurement use cases.
ASSUMPTIONS: Government agencies are willing to adopt blockchain technology.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Subject to regulatory approval and legal compliance.

CLAIM: The data points plotted in Figure 1 exhibit a correlation coefficient greater than 0.9 with a linear trendline.
ASSUMPTIONS: The data represented in Figure 1 is accurately plotted and represents the intended variables.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: This claim is limited to the specific data set and axes represented in Figure 1.

CLAIM: The data in Figure 1 exhibits a Pearson correlation coefficient greater than 0.9 with a linear function.
ASSUMPTIONS: Data in Figure 1 is accurate and representative.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Only applies to the specific data presented in Figure 1.

CLAIM: The data plotted in Figure 1 exhibits a linear relationship between the X and Y axes.
ASSUMPTIONS: Data points in Figure 1 are accurately represented; The scale of the axes is linear.
BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: The claim is valid only within the range of data presented in Figure 1.
